We had the entire facility to ourselves.
The on-site services were excellent and it was a wonderful facility.
I will definitely use it again.

I used the dog run, but there were no other users.
When I inquired by phone, I was told that "rescue dogs are playing," but there weren't any. When I arrived, they brought out one rescue puppy, but it was still on a leash.
That was all.
There were no toys, and no other dogs to play with.
My dog, who loves dog runs, wasn't happy at all.
When I said, "Let's go home," he was overjoyed... I was shocked.
It was completely pointless to go.

We used their services for our child's kindergarten.

There is inconsistency in the staff's service.

They provide no detailed explanations about the kindergarten's system or fees, and important information is only shared if you ask.

During drop-off and pick-up, they often lack the kind of attentiveness that is standard in other obedience classes, such as sharing information about the dog's condition or how well they ate that day.

The weekend events are excellent and well-organized.

I am a pet owner who has been a customer of your shop for many years. I was satisfied with your high-end pricing and trusted your "professional care," including your pick-up and drop-off service. However, my trust has completely crumbled after two visits in the last two months.

First blunder (last time):
My dog's fur was clearly wet when I returned home. When I called to inquire, I was simply told, "We'll be more careful next time," and that was the end of it. There was no compensation, not even a sincere response.

Second betrayal (today):
Not only was the "forgetting to dry" issue not resolved, but my dog ​​was returned with dried excrement stuck to his rear end (photo evidence attached). As a professional that boasts about hygiene management, this is utterly unacceptable!

Most unforgivable response:
During the phone call, all I got was "We'll check with the staff," but:
✖️ Specific measures to prevent recurrence
✖️ An apology from the person in charge
✖️ Compensation for services, etc.
── None of these were offered.

We demand a strict response:
1. An official apology from the person in charge
2. A full refund for the past two services
3. A complete review of the hygiene management manual

This post will be shared on all social media platforms. No more pet owners should have to go through the same thing. We absolutely cannot overlook this act that mocks the consumer contract of "high price = high quality."

This is a fairly large dog run in Tokyo. Dogly operates a hotel, grooming salon, animal hospital, and doggy daycare, so there are plenty of staff members, making it a safe and reliable place to use. (There are no staff members inside the dog run itself.) Part of the run is partitioned off to create a cafe-like area with tables where owners can relax, and there are machines in the hallway where you can freely get coffee and green tea, so it's very convenient. There are also chairs inside the run where you can put your belongings. The price is reasonable, around 900 yen per owner and one dog (the price increases if there are more people or dogs). It's nice that you get a chicken breast or liver treat when you use the run, and the underground parking lot is also convenient. However, for some reason there seems to be no anti-slip surface in the run, so when I threw a ball to my dog ​​it slid right off, which is why I'm deducting one star. Since it's a facility specializing in dogs, I would think that there must be some anti-slip surface, so maybe it's just peeled off. In any case, in this intense heat, an indoor dog run that is comfortable for both people and dogs is truly a blessing.

This review is solely about the dog run.

It's spacious, toys are available, and there's plenty of time to play without worrying about the clock, which is great on many days. The dogs seem to have a lot of fun chasing balls together. However, there are no staff members in the dog run, so there are many disappointing days.

There doesn't seem to be an age limit, so sometimes small children come, and the dogs in the run react to the children running around, leading to chases and the children screaming.

Also, some medium to large dogs from this shelter, who still have biting habits, come to the run. You can easily get bitten. If you encounter one of these dogs right after they arrive, you can barely play and have to retreat. There are no separate areas or time slots for different breeds. While it's understandable that dogs with biting habits can't go to other runs and that they can use the run from their original shelter, I wish there were at least some time restrictions.

Is this organization truly non-profit?

I was told that the chances of being accepted for a trial adoption depended on the amount of the adoption fee.

Before the trial, without any explanation whatsoever, I was told on the day of the trial that the child I had hoped for had already been adopted, without any prior notice.

This organization is completely untrustworthy.
